[Pedagogy review · pf-16eb3b71e6]
Before p33-polynomial-division-theory, rehearse the symbolic operations combined in the first division example:
(a) Simplify 3x²÷x and 8x³÷2x.
(b) Expand 3x(x−1).
(c) Expand −8(x−1).
(d) Simplify (3x²−11x+2)−(3x²−3x).
Answers: (a) 3x, 4x²; (b) 3x²−3x; (c) −8x+8; (d) −8x+2.

[Pedagogy review · pf-37db4565f8]
Before the remainder-theorem investigation, rehearse substitution: For F(x)=2x³−3x²+x−4, write the substituted expression, then evaluate (a) F(2), (b) F(−1), (c) F(½). Answers: 2, −10, −4. This separates substitution from the new connection between P(a) and the remainder.

[Pedagogy review · pf-c6d6515c57]
Append two follow-up parts to p57-q19: (b) Find the remainder when P(−x) is divided by x²−5. (c) Find the remainder when P(x)−P(−x) is divided by x²−5. Answers: (b) −x+4; (c) 2x. These compare cancellation in the existing sum with subtraction.

[Pedagogy review · pf-9cc07eca49]
Before the combined solving example at p60-teaching, add a short review: (a) Factorise x²+x−12. (b) Factorise 2x²−7x+3. (c) Solve (x+4)(2x−3)=0. Answers: (a) (x+4)(x−3); (b) (2x−1)(x−3); (c) x=−4 or 3/2. This rehearses the final two steps before combining them with root testing and division.

[Pedagogy review · pf-5821af1c5d]
After factorising p70-q23, add: “Hence sketch y=x⁴−x³−5x²+12, marking its intercepts.” Answer: both ends rise; y-intercept (0,12); the only x-intercept is (2,0), where the graph touches the axis and turns upwards. This connects the repeated factor with its graph.

[Pedagogy review · pf-29351a7cef]
After p42-q3-a, append: “Predict which part of your answer will change.” Divide by x−1: (i) x³+x²−2x; (ii) x³+x²−2x+1; (iii) x³+x²−2x−2. Answers: quotient x²+2x throughout; remainders 0, 1, −2. Follow with (x³+2x²−x+4)÷(x+1): quotient x²+x−2, remainder 6. The first three parts vary only the constant term.
